title: Local Constrained Bayesian Optimization
claim: Our method reaches better constrained objective values than competing baselines across synthetic and real-world tasks as evaluations accumulate.
layout: 2 rows of 3 line plots, shared legend on top, shaded bands
description: Two rows of three line plots share a legend at the top. The legend lists five methods: LCBO as a solid red line, SCBO as black dashes, CEI as blue dash-dot, HDSAFEBO as green dots, and EPBO as purple dash-dot-dot. The top row shows the 25D, 50D and 100D synthetic tasks. The bottom row shows the Truss, Beam and Halfcheetah real-world tasks. Each panel plots best feasible objective (y-axis, lower is better) against number of evaluations (x-axis, 0 to 1000). Lines show the median, and translucent bands of the same color show the interquartile range. The red LCBO curve drops fastest and ends lowest in nearly every panel. The baselines plateau higher. The gap is largest in the 100D synthetic and Beam panels. The eye goes first to the red curve at the bottom of each plot. The crop also contains a synthetic-task caption between the two rows.
caption: Optimization progress on real-world tasks. The plotting conventions and axes definitions are identical to Figure [ref].
abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) for high-dimensional constrained problems remains a significant challenge due to the curse of dimensionality. We propose Local Constrained Bayesian Optimization (LCBO), a novel framework tailored for such settings. Unlike trust-region methods that are prone to premature shrinking when confronting tight or complex constraints, LCBO leverages the differentiable landscape of constraint-penalized surrogates to alternate between rapid local descent and uncertainty-driven exploration. Theoretically, we prove that LCBO achieves a convergence rate for the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) residual that depends polynomially on the dimension $d$ for common kernels under mild assumptions, offering a rigorous alternative to global BO where regret bounds typically scale exponentially. Extensive evaluations on high-dimensional benchmarks (up to 100D) demonstrate that LCBO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
